=== FINDING 1 (blocking): the PR de-stales item 3 and leaves item 4 asserting
the contradictory, and false, pre-1.1 rule count. ===

Item 3, as corrected by this PR: "1.1 DONE, merged (commit 6afc545, #50)."
Item 4, eight lines below, untouched: "2 rules on `main` today (4 once 1.1
lands)."

Measured on origin/main (0d1be714ac028d9b2204bf997d49296c32378ff1):
  $ git ls-tree --name-only origin/main core/lwb_core/rules/
  core/lwb_core/rules/__init__.py
  core/lwb_core/rules/lwb_proof_coverage.py
  core/lwb_core/rules/lwb_proof_integrity.py
  core/lwb_core/rules/lwb_proof_required.py
  core/lwb_core/rules/lwb_version.py
=> FOUR rule modules on main today, not two. All four are registered in
core/lwb_core/rules/__init__.py's RULES list (lines 28-32).

The arithmetic confirms the parenthetical is the stale half, not the count:
build-plan.md:80 defines 1.1 as "Ship `proof_coverage` and `proof_integrity`
as rules". Pre-1.1 there were 2 (lwb_proof_required, lwb_version); 1.1 adds
exactly the 2 named; 2 + 2 = 4. "(4 once 1.1 lands)" was written before 1.1
landed and is now describing as future the very event item 3 declares done.

So after this PR merges, HANDOFF.md simultaneously says 1.1 has landed and
that main still carries the pre-1.1 rule count. That is the exact staleness
class this PR exists to remove, with the same root cause, left in place two
bullets away. Under directive 7a a stated project-state count must be backed
by a command actually run; this one contradicts the command above.

SUGGESTED FIX (prose only, no code): item 4 -> "0 of 13 stages, 4 rules on
`main` today, 0 armed to deny, 2 of 8 skills working." I did NOT re-verify
"0 of 13 stages", "0 armed to deny" or "2 of 8 skills working" (see
NOT CHECKED) -- only the rule count, which I measured.

=== FINDING 2 (blocking): "Auto-queue is `workflow_dispatch`-only" is false,
and the surrounding "outside any PR's diff / don't re-litigate" actively
steers the next session away from the open PR that fixes it. ===

New item 3 text: "waiting only on Auto-queue (`workflow_dispatch`-only, no
run in >24h -- flagged to owner on #45 as a structural hazard outside any
PR's diff, already escalated). None blocked; don't re-litigate."

Measured, `git show origin/main:.github/workflows/auto-queue.yml`:
  on:
    check_suite:
      types: [completed]
    workflow_dispatch:
      inputs: ...
The workflow declares TWO triggers. `check_suite: [completed]` has been
there since the file was created on 2026-09-19 (de27f72, PR #31 --
`git log -S'check_suite' origin/main -- .github/workflows/auto-queue.yml`).
It has never been `workflow_dispatch`-only.

The "no run in >24h" half IS true and I confirmed it:
  $ gh api .../actions/workflows/auto-queue.yml/runs?per_page=10
  total_count 6; most recent 2026-09-25T02:26:20Z; now 2026-09-26T05:00Z
  => ~26.5h. Also: all 6 runs ever recorded have event=workflow_dispatch;
  zero were check_suite-triggered.

So the behaviour ("only ever fires on dispatch") is real, but the stated
CAUSE ("`workflow_dispatch`-only") is wrong, and the two imply different
fixes: "add an automatic trigger" versus "the automatic trigger exists and
silently never fires". The second is the true one, and it is already
diagnosed IN THIS REPO -- open PR #64
(7026d309abcb11d65d1a0c940e899d22e3e74451, `lwb-recut-48-autoqueue-identity-fix`)
adds this comment to the same file:
  "`check_suite` never fires for a suite GitHub Actions itself created --
   a built-in recursion guard -- so the automatic path built on it never ran
   once, in this repo's entire history, while ~18 check suites completed on
   open PRs the same day (measured 2026-09-19). This is that defect's fix."
and replaces the trigger with `workflow_run` on CI/Handoff plus a 15-minute
`schedule`.

That makes "outside any PR's diff" false as written -- #64's diff is exactly
where it lives -- and #64 is omitted from item 3's list of open Phase-1 PRs
(1.2 #51, 1.4 #62, 1.5 #68, 1.6 #53, 1.7 #66, 1.8 #71). Paired with "None
blocked; don't re-litigate", a reader is told not to look at the one open PR
that unblocks the queue every other item is said to be waiting on.

SUGGESTED FIX: "waiting only on Auto-queue, whose `check_suite` trigger never
fires (GitHub's recursion guard on Actions-created suites); fix open as #64.
Last run 2026-09-25." Attribute the recursion-guard mechanism to #64's own
measurement, not to mine -- I confirmed 0 of 6 runs were check_suite-triggered
and that the trigger is declared, and I take #64's causal explanation on trust.

=== MUTATION PROBE: both false claims are unguarded. ===

I falsified each claim in the working tree and re-ran the gates that see
HANDOFF.md:
  (1) "2 rules on `main` today (4" -> "999 rules on `main` today (1234":
      lwb_check_state_claims.py exit=0, lwb_handoff.py --check exit=0.
  (2) "`workflow_dispatch`-only" -> "`schedule`-only-and-also-cron-every-second":
      lwb_check_state_claims.py exit=0, lwb_handoff.py --check exit=0.
  CONTROL, a claim the gate does cover -- generated-block "main SHA:" set to
  deadbeef...: lwb_check_state_claims.py exit=1,
  "FAIL: HANDOFF.md:46: [stale main SHA in generated block]".
The control fires, so the probe is not vacuous: the gates genuinely run and
genuinely cannot see either of my two findings. This is the documented
HONEST SCOPE limit of lwb_check_state_claims ("a claim that is stale but
phrased without any of the covered patterns... this is pattern matching, not
language understanding"), NOT a new defect introduced here -- but it means
nothing mechanical will catch either error, which is why they are blocking
on review rather than on CI. Working tree restored (`git diff --quiet` clean)
before writing this record.

=== NEAR-MISS I ALMOST FILED, RECORDED AS REQUIRED ===

On first reading auto-queue.yml I saw `on: check_suite: [completed]` at line
24 and was about to file "the PR calls it workflow_dispatch-only but the
trigger is check_suite" as a flat contradiction. Before writing it I printed
the full `on:` block and found `workflow_dispatch` IS also declared (lines
26-31), and then pulled the run history and found the behavioural claim
(dispatch-only in practice, nothing in >24h) is empirically TRUE. Had I
stopped at line 25 I would have accused the author of inventing the
dispatch-only observation, when what is actually wrong is narrower: the
observation is right and the mechanism attributed to it is wrong. Finding 2
is written to that narrower, correct scope.

I also nearly filed "HANDOFF's generated block says `Open PRs: (unavailable:
no gh auth in this environment, or no open PRs)` while 15 PRs are open" as a
defect of this PR -- the repo's own item-5 defect pattern, "I could not
check" sharing a representation with "I checked and found nothing". I did
not file it: that line is byte-identical on origin/main, is produced by
lwb_handoff.py which this PR does not touch, and the generator genuinely had
no gh auth. It is a real pre-existing wart in a shared path, worth its own
PR, but it is not this PR's to answer and I am not holding this PR for it.
